messages.content: Let's compare the Washington dates before we get into hotels. It would be me, Daniel, and Owen. We can leave Thursday evening or Friday morning, but either way we need to come back Monday evening.
What are the exact dates, and are you looking at O'Hare, Midway, or both?
Thursday October 10 versus Friday October 11, returning Monday October 14. Start with O'Hare. Nonstop only. We want enough actual time for the Smithsonian museums and a day around the monuments.

I found two workable nonstop structures for all three of you.

Thursday-Monday: American leaves O'Hare Thursday at 5:05 p.m. and arrives at Reagan National at 7:58 p.m. The Monday return leaves DCA at 6:15 p.m. and reaches O'Hare at 7:36 p.m. Total airfare is $1,074, or $358 each.

Friday-Monday: American leaves O'Hare Friday at 8:10 a.m. and arrives at DCA at 11:03 a.m. It uses the same Monday return. Total airfare is $897, or $299 each.

The first pattern requires four hotel nights; the second requires three.
How much usable time do we really gain Thursday? Don't count Thursday night as sightseeing time if we're just getting to the hotel.

The gain is mainly Friday morning and a less rushed start. With the Thursday flight, you should reach a central hotel around 8:45-9:15 p.m., so Friday can begin when museums open around 10:00 a.m.

With the Friday flight, a realistic sequence is landing at 11:03, reaching the hotel around noon, leaving bags, and starting around 12:30-1:00 p.m. That costs roughly 2.5 to 3 hours of Friday sightseeing. Thursday evening itself adds no meaningful touring time.
And Monday? I don't want the evening return to turn into a wasted day because we have luggage.

Monday remains useful with either pattern. A hotel in Penn Quarter, near Archives, or around the Convention Center should hold your bags after checkout. You could sightsee until about 3:30 p.m., retrieve them, and leave for DCA around 4:00. That provides about two hours at the airport for the 6:15 departure.
So lay out the actual trip duration, not just the number of nights.

Thursday-Monday is four nights and about 98.5 hours from scheduled arrival at DCA to scheduled departure from DCA. In practical touring terms, it gives you three full days, Friday through Sunday, plus most of Monday.

Friday-Monday is three nights and about 79 hours on the same basis. It gives you Friday afternoon, two full days on Saturday and Sunday, and most of Monday.
That makes the Thursday option sound like almost another day, but you said the real difference is only three hours.

Correct. The raw trip duration differs by about 19.5 hours because Thursday includes an overnight period. Once sleep, the transfer, and breakfast are removed, the additional usable sightseeing is approximately 2.5 to 3 hours on Friday morning. Its other benefit is arriving rested rather than starting the trip with an early flight.
What does that extra time cost once we add the fourth hotel night? Use a realistic central-hotel range, not a teaser rate.

The Thursday airfare costs $177 more for the three of you. For the areas that fit this itinerary, a realistic fourth-night estimate is $285-$345 including tax for one room. That puts the total premium for Thursday travel at roughly $462-$522.

Effectively, you would be paying about $154-$174 per added sightseeing hour, though the rested Friday start is part of what that premium buys.
One room is fine, but it needs to sleep three without assuming a rollaway. Which areas are you using for that estimate?

Penn Quarter/Chinatown, the Convention Center area, and the blocks near Archives are the best assumptions for the next hotel comparison. They keep you near multiple Metro lines and within a reasonable walk or short ride of the National Mall. The estimate assumes a room explicitly listed with two queen beds or another confirmed three-person sleeping configuration, not a king room with a possible rollaway.
Would the Wharf be better for the monuments day?

It can work, especially for the Jefferson Memorial and the southern end of the Mall, but it is less balanced for several museum visits and evening access to restaurants away from the waterfront. For this trip, Penn Quarter or Archives is the stronger all-around base. The Wharf should stay in the comparison only if a clearly better room or total price appears.
Any arrival problem with Thursday beyond getting in late? Owen will still have school that day, and I can't assume we're at O'Hare at four.

That is the main weakness. For the 5:05 p.m. flight, you would want to be at O'Hare around 3:35 p.m. If school pickup or work makes that uncertain, the flight has little margin. There is a 7:20 p.m. nonstop arriving DCA at 10:13 p.m., but it costs $1,143 total and likely puts you at the hotel around 11:15. That preserves Friday morning but makes the extra night less comfortable and raises the premium further.
Drop the 5:05, then. Compare the 7:20 Thursday flight directly with Friday morning. Same Monday flight.

Thursday 7:20 p.m.-Monday 6:15 p.m.: $1,143 total airfare, four hotel nights, hotel arrival around 11:00-11:30 p.m., and a full Friday beginning around 10:00 a.m. Against the Friday plan, it adds $246 in airfare plus an estimated $285-$345 hotel night, so the total premium is about $531-$591.

Friday 8:10 a.m.-Monday 6:15 p.m.: $897 total airfare, three hotel nights, hotel arrival around noon, and sightseeing beginning around 12:30-1:00 p.m. It is cheaper and avoids the late hotel arrival, but Friday is a partial day.
Can we still do two museum-heavy days and one monuments day with Friday morning?

Yes. Use Friday afternoon for one focused museum, Saturday for two Smithsonian museums or one large museum plus a shorter stop, Sunday for the monuments and memorials, and Monday morning through midafternoon for the remaining museum. Timed-entry availability could change the order, but the Friday-Monday pattern has enough usable time without forcing the Thursday night.
Then keep Friday as the value option and Thursday as the fallback if timed entries make Friday morning important. Give me the two structures cleanly so we can compare hotels next.

Value option: Friday, October 11, American nonstop from O'Hare at 8:10 a.m., arriving DCA at 11:03 a.m.; return Monday, October 14, at 6:15 p.m., arriving O'Hare at 7:36 p.m. Airfare for three is $897. This is a three-night stay with sightseeing from about 12:30-1:00 p.m. Friday through about 3:30 p.m. Monday.

Fallback: Thursday, October 10, American nonstop at 7:20 p.m., arriving DCA at 10:13 p.m.; same Monday return. Airfare for three is $1,143. This is a four-night stay, with hotel arrival around 11:00-11:30 p.m. and a full Friday available. Including the extra hotel night, it is estimated to cost $531-$591 more than the Friday plan.

For the hotel comparison, start with Penn Quarter/Chinatown, Archives, and the Convention Center area. Price one room with a confirmed sleeping setup for three and include all taxes. Keep the Wharf only as a price or room-quality alternative. Nothing has been booked.
